definitions.explanation: Low in price. A somewhat old-fashioned usage.
Taking the easy way without much thought or effort. Often carries a critical nuance of being too simple-minded or lazy in approach.

examples.japanese: {安直|あんちょく}な{値段|ねだん}で{買|か}えた。
examples.english: I was able to buy it at a cheap price.

examples.japanese: もう{少|すこ}し{安直|あんちょく}な{店|みせ}はないかな。
examples.english: I wonder if there's a cheaper shop.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}はこの{辺|あた}りは{物価|ぶっか}が{安直|あんちょく}だった。
examples.english: Prices used to be cheap around here in the old days.

examples.japanese: {安直|あんちょく}な{考|かんが}えは{危険|きけん}だ。
{安直|あんちょく}に{結論|けつろん}を{出|だ}すべきではない。
examples.english: You shouldn't jump to a conclusion too easily.

examples.japanese: {安直|あんちょく}な{方法|ほうほう}に{頼|たよ}ると、あとで{後悔|こうかい}することになる。
examples.english: If you rely on an easy approach, you'll end up regretting it later.

notes: Sense 1 (cheap/inexpensive) is somewhat dated and rarely used in modern conversation. Sense 2 (easy/simplistic) is the more common modern usage and almost always carries a negative nuance — it criticizes a lack of serious thought or effort. Common collocations: {安直|あんちょく}な{考|かんが}え (simplistic thinking), {安直|あんちょく}に{考|かんが}える (to think too simply), {安直|あんちょく}な{方法|ほうほう} (an easy/lazy method).
